name: Collision Probe
summary: Not a useful module: a live manifest demonstrating three unenforced extension-point ambiguities.
description: Declares two `command` extension points both named `probe`, gated on different permissions (`see-public`, `see-admin`); only the first-declared one is ever checked by http::module_commands::required_permission, and the second is silently dead. Also declares a `slash-command` named `co llide` - an embedded space that manifest validation accepts but the composer's whitespace-splitting keyword match can never invoke - alongside a working `probe` alias. Built to find the edges of what a manifest may declare without the install path, the runtime, or the client ever objecting.
author: slim-m

permissions.name: See public
permissions.description: The permission actually enforced for /probe - it is declared first.

permissions.name: See admin
permissions.description: Declared on the second, identically named command extension point. Never enforced: this permission grants nothing, because the runtime only ever consults the first command extension point of a given name.

extension_points.name: probe
extension_points.description: Declared first: this is the permission every /modules/collision-probe/commands/probe call is actually gated on.

extension_points.name: probe
extension_points.description: Declared second, same name as the command above. Dead weight: this permission is never consulted for anything.

extension_points.name: co llide
extension_points.description: An embedded space. Installs cleanly, but the composer's own keyword split on whitespace means this can never be typed or matched.
